newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan auto output up for first time in six years.
newsitem.headline: Japan auto output up for first time in six years.

text.p: Japan's vehicle output rose in the just ended financial year for the first time in six years, according to figures released on Friday.
The rise came from robust exports and strong demand ahead of an April 1 sales tax rise.
The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) said that output rose 5.2 percent from a year earlier to 10.61 million units in the year to March 1997.
Japan' exports had started marking gains on year-on-year basis since June last year because of weak yen after posting declines for 17 straight months.
Domestic sales in January to March rose sharply as consumers rushed to buy ahead of a April 1 rise in Japan's sales tax to five percent from the previous three percent.

"Japan's vehicle production this business year will exceed last year because Japanese exports are expected to increase not only for the United States but other areas in view of the weak yen," said Nikko Research senior analyst Noriyuki Matsushima.
Nikko Research estimated Japan's vehicle production in 1997/98 at just below 11 million units, largely in line with JAMA's estimate made in March.

But Matsushima said rising Japanese car exports are unlikely to be the key trade issue with the United States for the time being because sales and profits of the U.S. Big Three are in good shape due to a healthy American economy, Matsushima said.
Last week, U.S. trade officials expressed concerns about rising Japanese car imports into the U.S. market.
